task.description:
ADHOC infrastructure blocker (Infrastructure Health Checklist, docs/guides/test_infrastructure_guide.md section 3) before TEST-RUNNER can be dispatched for WF03-GH716-20260812 (GH-716 / ISS-0675 / PAR-06 dead-code removal). `zig build test-env-verify` currently returns UNHEALTHY (exit 1), 3 of 10 checks failed:

C1 db_test container healthy: 'r-co-db_test-1 is healthy but does not publish port 5453 from BPM_TEST_DB_URL (postgres://bpm:***@localhost:5453/bpm_test) — the healthy container is not the database the tests connect to'. Remedy suggested by the tool: align COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME and BPM_TEST_DB_URL's port (see .env).

C3 zig build migrate: 'migrate exited 0 but postgres://bpm:***@localhost:5453/bpm_test has 135 applied migration(s) for schema_name=public while migrations/ contains 134 *.sql file(s) (delta = 1) — the test database is not fully migrated'.

C4 schema baseline: same delta=1 finding via check_migration_ledger_count.

Remedy suggested by the tool for C3/C4: python3 tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants --auto-fix

IMPORTANT CONTEXT: BACKEND-DEV's own Step 03 of this same run (immediately prior) successfully ran `zig build test-integration-par06` (3/3 pass), `zig build test-integration-par06-reconstruction` (5/5 pass), and the full `zig build test` suite (1071/1135 pass, 64 pre-existing skips) against this exact same test database just minutes before this check ran — so C1's port-mismatch complaint may be a config-drift-detector false positive rather than an actual connectivity failure (the tests DID connect and pass). Investigate C1 first: confirm whether BPM_TEST_DB_URL in .env, docker-compose.yml, and any docker-compose.override.yml actually agree on port 5453/5434 and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, and whether the check itself has a stale assumption. Do NOT rename/reformat the check's output to make it stop matching (core-directives.md's 'never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures') — if C1 is a genuine detector bug, fix tools/verify_test_env.py's C1 logic; if it is a real config drift, fix .env/docker-compose. C3/C4 (migration ledger delta=1) is likely a real, separate condition — run the suggested remedy (python3 tools/verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants --auto-fix) and confirm it resolves cleanly without silently dropping/altering unrelated schema state. This environment issue is unrelated to the GH-716 code change itself (which already passed its own tests) — this is a pre-existing infrastructure gap that must be fixed before TEST-RUNNER can run the full pipeline per the mandatory pre-check in docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md.
acceptance_criteria: zig build test-env-verify exits 0 (HEALTHY, all 10 checks pass)
Root cause of C1/C3/C4 identified and fixed at the source, not the detector silenced
No unrelated schema/data loss from the auto-fix remedy

result.summary: Root cause of C1/C3/C4 was a single stale Windows User-scope environment variable BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test (port 5453, the sibling worktree r-co-2 COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME band), left over from earlier work in the .claude/worktrees/agent-af4ebe759e4b7ed6d checkout. Per verify_test_env.py's documented and intentional precedence (process environment always wins, .env fills gaps only — ISS-0151/GH#468, matching bench.zig resolveDbUrl), this stale value shadowed .env's correct BPM_TEST_DB_URL=...:5434/bpm_test for every new process, so C1 correctly reported that the healthy container (r-co-db_test-1 on 5434) was not the one named by BPM_TEST_DB_URL, and C3/C4 migrated/counted against the wrong database (r-co-2-db_test-1 on port 5453, which legitimately has 135 migrations applied because it is ahead on its own branch) instead of this workspace's db_test. This was NOT a bug in verify_test_env.py (its process-env-wins precedence is correct and intentional) and NOT a real migration/ledger drift in this workspace (confirmed 134/134 once pointed at the right DB) — so no auto-fix/ledger edit was needed or run. Fix: cleared the stale BPM_TEST_DB_URL, BPM_IDP_BASE_URL, BPM_TEST_URL from HKCU\Environment (Windows User scope) via [System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable (confirmed via reg query afterward: all three now absent from HKCU\Environment). This is a pure machine-local environment fix — no .env, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.override.yml, or tools/verify_test_env.py changes were made or needed. Residual finding for the record: this session's own shell processes (bash.exe/powershell.exe under the existing VS Code/Code.exe ancestor, PID 21008) keep the old value cached in their inherited process environment block until that ancestor is restarted — confirmed the HKCU registry value itself is clean via reg query, and that new/independent process launches (Start-Process, fresh powershell.exe -NoProfile) read the corrected value; the caching is a session artifact of the already-running IDE process tree, not an unresolved config problem. Verified zig build test-env-verify (HEALTHY, 10/10 checks pass, exit 0), zig build test-integration-par06 (3/3 pass, exit 0), and zig build test-integration-par06-reconstruction (5/5 pass, exit 0) all green with BPM_TEST_DB_URL correctly resolved to port 5434.

issues.description: This session's bash.exe/powershell.exe tool processes (children of the existing VS Code Code.exe, PID 21008) retain the stale BPM_TEST_DB_URL (port 5453) in their own inherited process environment even after the HKCU\Environment registry fix, because they were already running before the fix was applied and do not re-read the registry. Any zig build test-* / test-env-verify invocation in a NEW shell/session in this workspace picks up the corrected value automatically; within this already-running session, BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5434/bpm_test must be explicitly exported before invoking zig build (unsetting it entirely is NOT sufficient, since zig build test-integration-* does not itself fall back to .env the way verify_test_env.py does — confirmed by reproducing 0/3 and 0/5 test failures (MissingTestDatabaseUrl) when the var was unset rather than corrected). TEST-RUNNER's next dispatch should be a fresh process and should not need this workaround, but if it inherits this same session it will need the same explicit export.

result.next_action: Route to TEST-RUNNER (services healthy, PAR-06 tests reconfirmed passing)
